meta.scope: Paraguay batch 4 — Itaipú royalties & energy fiscal flows, public debt, tax collection, maquila/zonas francas industrial depth, and investment promotion. Pushing toward ~50-candidate depth.

candidates.title: Royalties y compensación por cesión de energía (Itaipú)
candidates.description: Fiscal transfers from Itaipú to the Paraguayan state under the Treaty Annex C: royalties and compensation for energy ceded to Brazil. Major non-tax revenue stream distributed to the central government, departments and municipalities.
candidates.notes: Structural fiscal node unique to Paraguay. Hundreds of millions of USD annually (e.g. ~USD 400–500 mn range in recent full years). Part funds the national budget; part is transferred to subnational governments and social funds (e.g. FONAE for school feeding).

candidates.title: Deuda pública / Public debt statistics
candidates.description: Stock and flow statistics of central-government and public-sector debt (external and domestic). Key sustainability indicator.
candidates.notes: Critical fiscal-sustainability node. Mid-2026 stock around USD 22 bn (~34% of GDP in recent readings). Continuously monitored in macroeconomic and policy analysis.

candidates.title: Subsecretaría de Estado de Tributación (SET) — tax collection
candidates.description: National tax administration. Publishes tax collection by type of tax (income tax, VAT, etc.) and performance against annual targets.
candidates.notes: Primary non-energy revenue-side fiscal statistic. Complements customs revenue and the energy royalty stream.

candidates.title: Ingresos fiscales del Estado / Consolidated fiscal revenues
candidates.description: Consolidated view of central-government revenues including tax, customs, energy royalties/compensation and other non-tax income.
candidates.notes: Operational revenue dashboard. Links the real-side economy (taxes, trade) and the binational energy complex to the financing of the national budget.

candidates.title: Régimen de Zonas Francas
candidates.publisher: MIC / Consejo Nacional de Zonas Francas
candidates.description: Free-zone regime offering tax and customs incentives for industrial, commercial and services activities.
candidates.notes: Complementary industrial-promotion instrument to the maquila regime. Smaller employment footprint than maquila but strategically important for logistics and specific manufacturing.

candidates.title: Ley 60/90 — Régimen de promoción de inversiones
candidates.description: General investment-promotion law granting tax and customs benefits for declared investment projects (capital-goods import exemptions, etc.).
candidates.notes: Core horizontal investment-incentive framework. Continuously cited alongside the maquila regime as a reason firms locate in Paraguay.

candidates.title: REDIEX — Red de Inversiones y Exportaciones
candidates.description: National investment and export promotion network/agency. Publishes investor guides, sector profiles and trade intelligence.
candidates.notes: Institutional interface between the incentive regimes (maquila, Law 60/90, free zones) and private investors and exporters.

candidates.title: Departamento de Alto Paraná — industrial & border hub
candidates.description: Eastern border department containing Ciudad del Este. Major commercial, industrial and re-export hub; intermediate poverty relative to the northern departments.
candidates.notes: Completes the economic-geography set. Hosts significant maquila and commercial activity; poverty lower than the northern interior but higher than Asunción/Central.

candidates.title: Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS) — social-security coverage
candidates.description: Main social-security institution covering pensions, health insurance and other benefits for formal workers. Major formal-employment and social-protection actor.
candidates.notes: Central formal-employment and social-protection node. Cotizante counts and benefit statistics complement the EPHC labour series; health coverage remains a major policy issue (large share of population without formal insurance).

candidates.title: Fondo Nacional de Alimentación Escolar (FONAE)
candidates.description: National school-feeding fund financed in part by Itaipú energy-compensation transfers. Links the energy-fiscal stream to a core social programme.
candidates.notes: Illustrative social-programme node. Receives a large share of the Itaipú compensation-for-energy-cession resources under the current distribution law.

proposed_edges.basis: Royalties and compensation flows originate from the Itaipú binational entity under the Treaty Annex C.
A material share of royalty and compensation resources enters the national budget and subnational transfers.
FONAE is a primary destination of Itaipú compensation-for-energy-cession resources.
Tax collection is a core component of consolidated fiscal revenues.
Public-debt dynamics are inseparable from the financing of the national budget.
REDIEX promotes and explains the Law 60/90 incentive regime to investors.
Maquila and free-zone regimes are complementary industrial-promotion instruments.
IPS administrative data on formal contributors complement the household-survey labour series.
